scope: Integrated research prototype, NOT the production frontend or a syntax cutover. All observed regressions are preserved. Shared A0 source/spec grammar, typing and verification execute in Wasm; a generic host schema adapter supplies typed IR to the same public backends. No source reparse or host revalidation. Compilation time and memory fail selection; no superiority or no-regression claim.
baseline: Six frozen flattened graphs used by the earlier C-analysis matrices, linked from the feature research corpus. Static 43-unit token baseline has a different, explicitly recorded source freeze. These timings do not include graph loading, shipping CLI startup, formatter/model costs, native C compilation or target execution.

candidate.singleA0Grammar: Same source implementation in seed-built, public optimized-C and private aggregate-ABI builds. Internal build artifacts differ; source syntax and frontend logic do not.
candidate.remaining: Authoritative formatter, graph loader, full diagnostic mapping, resource/stack/lifetime audits, migration/tooling integration and performance repair.

environment.conditions: Quiet rotating fresh-process comparisons, one warmup/seven measured rounds, recorded loads and output SHA checks, no simultaneous builds/tests/model collectors. All arms equally preload reference modules and compiled Wasm. Raw Wasm/IR result retained during C emission.

dependencies.provenance: Verified against signed Debian APT metadata and extracted into a private sysroot. Libraries are external dependencies, not bundled in the research export; artifact distribution needs their applicable notices.

defaultC.scope: Default C emission remains byte-identical to committed scoped-analysis backend. Both A0 optimization settings, whole-program/independent corpus and strict kernel controls. The new host I/O ABI is opt-in; no change to default generated output.

programs.name: arith
programs.about: u32 arithmetic wraps mod 2^32; div and rem are total; shifts use the low five bits

programs.name: logic
programs.about: bool logic, comparisons (unsigned), select computes both arms

programs.name: array
programs.about: array values: get reduces the index modulo the length, set returns a copy

programs.name: record
programs.about: records: rec, at, put (a copy), records inside arrays and arrays inside records

programs.name: iterate
programs.about: fold and loop: zero trips, extras, early stop by predicate, aggregate state, nesting

programs.name: calls
programs.about: call chains and the call/ID shorthand, callee results feeding callers

programs.name: bigret
programs.about: a u32 literal of 2^28 or more as the ret operand (the IR ret word packs 28 bits; larger literals are a kind-5 operand), alone and through callers

programs.name: biglit
programs.about: u32 literals of 2^28 or more (past the 28-bit value of the packed ret word) as add, xor, compare and select operands, fold initial states, literal-only calls the optimizer evaluates, and select operands at the ret

programs.name: text
programs.about: text literals are arrays of UTF-8 bytes with escapes

programs.name: io
programs.about: io tokens order effects: read (0 when exhausted), write, puts, folds that thread the stream

programs.name: checked
programs.about: the total checked ops return (value, ok): cadd/csub/cmul flag overflow, cdiv/crem a zero divisor, cget an index at or past the length

programs.name: strict_checked
programs.about: the checked ops give the same values under profile strict, and never trap

programs.name: strict_index
programs.about: profile strict: get/set at or past the length trap bounds (a dead get too, and a get in the untaken select arm), an index proved in range does not

programs.name: strict_div
programs.about: profile strict: div/rem by zero trap divzero (a dead div too); a divisor proved nonzero does not; the first trap in node order wins

programs.name: strict_wrap
programs.about: profile strict: add, sub, mul and the shifts still wrap and mask; they never trap

programs.name: strict_iterate
programs.about: profile strict: a trap in a fold or loop body names the node, the trip and the call chain; an aggregate-state fold updated in place traps before it writes

programs.name: strict_io
programs.about: profile strict: a read after the last input word traps input (inside a fold too); within the input it reads as usual

programs.name: chainrot
programs.about: chains of one associative op (add, mul, xor, and, or) whose late operand is a product: the optimizer rotates the chain so the late operand joins last (a latency model, no change of value), with literals, shared inner nodes and chains through calls

Canonical/Dense/unified reference/unified A0, exact Dense conversion validated outside timing; same frozen graphs and C output. Rebuilt direct-host Wasm is byte-identical to the private measured artifact.

hostBoundary.scope: Exploratory phase profile only; three trials without matched arms, not a performance comparison or selection gate.

a0Phases.scope: Exploratory phase instrumentation of the same A0 frontend, direct host stream. Three in-process trials, not a matched latency comparison or selection gate. parseMs includes lexer and verifier initialization; verifyMs is remaining typed/spec evaluation.

exploratoryProfiles.scope: Three in-process trials for diagnosis only, not matched latency claims. parseMs includes token indexing and verifier initialization; remaining verifier time includes typing/spec evaluation.

decision: Do not cut over. The direct-host A0 frontend still loses compilation time and peak memory against Canonical in the published matched run. The private aggregate threshold trades smaller Wasm and memory in some cells for slower large inputs; it remains unpromoted. Keep grammar/migration work incremental and repair measured costs before removing existing readers or public tools.
